question: Which sea is the north-western part of the Indian Ocean that covers a total area of approximately 14,91,000 square miles and forms a part of the major sea route between Europe and India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arabian Sea.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Arabian Sea is to the northwest and the Andaman Sea is to the northeast.
 
• The Arabian Sea is the Northwestern part of the Indian Ocean, lying between India and the Arabian Peninsula. 
 
• It has an area of about** 1,491,000 sq miles (3,862,000 sq km)** and an average depth of **8,970 feet (2,734 m).**
 
• The Arabian Sea is named after the Arabian merchants who dominated the sea from the **9th century** to the late medieval period of history.
 
• Mumbai is located on the West Coast of India. Bounded by India, the Arabian Sea is a region of the Indian Ocean.
